subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The onEntryChange callback does `setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev }))` — it spreads the previous state into a new object with NO new data. This is a no-op that triggers a re-render but never changes any content value. No live preview data is ever merged into the context. The prescribed fix requires merging incoming draft content so that useContent→getContentByKey returns preview data instead of published data. This fails every acceptance criterion about reflecting updated values, navigation bar updates, and isolating unchanged entries.
issues.suggestedFix: The SDK's onEntryChange callback signature is () => void (confirmed via resolve_package_symbol — it does not pass entry data to the callback). After the callback fires, you must query the SDK for the updated entry data and merge it into the context value. For example, call ContentstackLivePreview.entry (or the SDK's equivalent getState/getEntry method) to retrieve the draft content, then setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev, page: [...updatedPage], livePreviewData: { ...prev.livePreviewData, [entryUid]: updatedEntry } })). At minimum, the callback must produce a context value that differs from the previous one by incorporating the preview payload.

issues.description: ContentstackProvider is exported but never wired into the application. All existing consumers (useContent.ts, MobileNav.tsx, TopBar.tsx, PageHead.tsx, etc.) call useContext(ContentstackContext) directly — none import or use ContentstackProvider. The useEffect that subscribes to live preview events lives inside ContentstackProvider, so the subscription never runs. The live preview integration is dead code.
issues.suggestedFix: Either wrap the application (or the relevant layout component) with <ContentstackProvider initialValue={fetchedContent}> at the app entry point, or move the onEntryChange subscription into the existing context provider that already wraps the app. If the app already fetches content and provides it via ContentstackContext.Provider elsewhere, add the subscription there instead of creating a new unused Provider.

issues.description: @contentstack/live-preview-utils is installed in node_modules but NOT declared in package.json (dependency_available reports 'installed_undeclared'). The build passes locally and CI because the package is on disk, but a clean install or production deploy will fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Add @contentstack/live-preview-utils to the dependencies array in package.json with the appropriate version.

issues.description: livePreviewData field is added to IContentstackContext but is never populated or consumed anywhere in the diff. It is dead code that does not fulfill the prescribed fix of carrying live preview state in the context.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the field (if the merge strategy overwrites existing fields like page/header directly) or actually populate it in the onEntryChange callback and have useContent/getValue read from it as a fallback layer.

issues.description: No unit tests were verified for the new ContentstackProvider or live preview subscription behavior. The git state shows src/context/contentstackContext.spec.ts was staged as a new file, but the core logic (no-op state update, unwired provider) means no test could pass the acceptance criteria. The prescribed behavior — entry change triggers context update, components re-render with preview data, other entries unchanged, disconnect preserves last values — requires test coverage mirroring src/context/contentstackContext.tsx.
issues.suggestedFix: Add vitest unit tests in src/context/contentstackContext.spec.ts that: (1) mock ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange, simulate an entry change, and assert the context value updates with preview data; (2) assert components reading a different entry remain unchanged; (3) assert navigation bar content updates; (4) assert that outside a preview session, published values display; (5) assert that on SDK error/disconnect, last values persist.

issues.description: The useContentstack hook's guard `if (!context)` is dead code. createContext<IContentstackContext>({}) provides a non-null default empty object, so useContext always returns a truthy value. The throw will never execute.
issues.suggestedFix: Either use a null sentinel: createContext<IContentstackContext | null>(null) and check `if (!context)`, or remove the guard entirely since the existing pattern in this codebase (useContent.ts) already calls useContext(ContentstackContext) directly without a guard.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The `onEntryChange` callback does `setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev }))` — a shallow copy of the same state with NO new data merged. The prescribed fix requires merging incoming draft content so that `useContent→getContentByKey` returns preview data instead of published data. This callback is a no-op: it triggers a re-render with identical values. The `livePreviewData` field added to `IContentstackContext` is never populated by the SDK callback, and `getContentByKey` (via `getValue`) traverses paths like `page.0.title` — it has no knowledge of `livePreviewData` and no merge logic overlays preview data onto published fields.
issues.suggestedFix: The `onEntryChange` callback must actually merge the incoming entry data into the context. Since the SDK's `onEntryChange` callback signature takes no arguments (confirmed via resolve_package_symbol: `OnEntryChangeCallback` is `() => void`), the SDK presumably patches the response objects in place or provides data through another mechanism. Investigate how the Contentstack Live Preview SDK delivers updated entry data (e.g., via `ContentstackLivePreview.getData()`, or by intercepting API responses), and in the callback, fetch the updated entry and merge it into the context value so that existing path-based lookups via `getValue` return the preview data. For example: `setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev, page: [updatedEntry] }))` or deep-merge the changed entry into the relevant top-level field.

issues.description: `ContentstackProvider` is dead code — codegraph_query for `ContentstackProvider` returned zero callers. The existing context consumers (`useContent`, `useDirectory`, `usePageBaseURLs`, `MobileNav`, `TopBar`, `PageHead`, etc.) all call `useContext(ContentstackContext)` directly and are NOT wrapped in `ContentstackProvider`. Without wrapping the app tree in this provider, the `onEntryChange` subscription in its `useEffect` never runs, and no live preview data ever reaches consumers. The diff adds a provider but does not integrate it anywhere in the app.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) wire `ContentstackProvider` into the app's root layout (e.g., `_app.tsx` or equivalent Next.js wrapper) so it wraps all consumers, passing the existing context data as `initialValue`; OR (b) add the `onEntryChange` subscription to wherever the context is currently populated (the existing provider/wrapper that feeds `ContentstackContext`), avoiding the new provider entirely. Option (b) is more concise and follows the prescribed minimal fix more closely.

issues.description: The `livePreviewData` field on `IContentstackContext` is never populated by any code path and is never read by `getContentByKey`/`getValue`. The prescribed fix says 'useContent→getContentByKey returns the preview data instead of the published data' — but `getValue(content, path, defaultValue)` traverses the context object by dot-path (e.g., `page.0.title`). Adding a separate `livePreviewData` map does not cause `getValue` to return preview data for existing paths. The field is dead weight that gives a false impression of compliance.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `livePreviewData` from the interface. Instead, merge the incoming preview entry data directly into the existing top-level fields (`page`, `header`, `footer`, etc.) so that `getValue` naturally returns the updated values when traversing the same paths the components already use.

issues.description: CONCISION & REUSE: The diff adds 35+ lines of new code (a provider component, a new `useContentstack` hook, a new `IContentstackProviderProps` interface) that are all unused dead code. A more concise change: add only the `onEntryChange` subscription + data-merge logic to the existing location where `ContentstackContext` is populated (the existing provider or page wrapper that sets the context value). This would be ~10 lines and would actually connect to the existing consumer tree. The new `useContentstack` hook (lines 51-53) duplicates what `useContent` already does (`useContext(ContentstackContext)`) and is never imported anywhere.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `ContentstackProvider`, `IContentstackProviderProps`, and `useContentstack`. Instead, find the existing code that populates `ContentstackContext` (the component or page that provides the context value) and add the `onEntryChange` subscription there, merging incoming entry data into the context state.

issues.description: Tests pass by mutating `initialValue` directly before firing the callback, relying on the fact that `setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev }))` preserves nested object references. This tests that React re-renders on a state reference change, NOT that the provider receives and merges live preview data from the SDK. In a real scenario, the SDK would deliver new entry data through its own mechanism — the tests don't verify that the provider correctly processes and merges that data. The test at line 73 (`initialValue.livePreviewData!.entryUid1 = { title: 'Updated' }`) mutates the source object, which is an anti-pattern that masks the fact that the provider never independently receives data.
issues.suggestedFix: Mock the SDK to deliver updated entry data through whatever mechanism the real SDK uses (e.g., mock a `getData()` return value or intercept the API response). Then verify the provider merges that data into context so `getContentByKey` returns the updated value — without pre-mutating the initial state.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The `onEntryChange` callback does `setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev }))` — a shallow copy of the same state with NO new data merged. The Contentstack Live Preview SDK's `onEntryChange` callback receives no arguments and does NOT mutate the context object in place (verified via resolve_package_symbol: `onEntryChange(callback: OnEntryChangeCallback)` — the callback signature takes no parameters). The comment claiming 'The SDK mutates the context object in place' is factually wrong. The prescribed root-cause fix requires merging incoming draft content into the context value so that `useContent→getContentByKey→getValue` returns preview data instead of published data. This callback is a no-op that triggers a re-render with identical values. None of the 5 verification criteria are met: changed entries do not update (VC1), unchanged entries trivially 'remain unchanged' because nothing changes (VC2), nav bar does not update (VC3), and disconnection/error resilience is moot since no data ever flows (VC5).
issues.suggestedFix: Call the SDK's API inside the `onEntryChange` callback to fetch the updated entry data, then deep-merge that draft content into the context value at the correct path (e.g., `page[0]`). For example: `defaultExport.onEntryChange(() => { const updatedEntry = defaultExport.getEntryData?.() /* or whatever the SDK exposes */; setValue((prev) => ({ ...prev, page: [{ ...prev.page?.[0], ...updatedEntry }] })); });`. The merge must overlay draft fields onto the existing published content so `getValue(content, 'page.0.title')` returns the preview value.

issues.description: `ContentstackProvider` is dead code — codegraph_query for `ContentstackProvider` returned zero results (symbol not found, zero callers). The provider is never imported or rendered anywhere in the app tree. Without wrapping the app (e.g., in `src/pages/[[...slug]].tsx` or `_app.tsx`), the `onEntryChange` subscription in its `useState` initializer never runs, and no live preview data ever reaches consumers. The existing context consumers (`useContent`, `useDirectory`, `MobileNav`, `TopBar`, `PageHead`, etc.) all call `useContext(ContentstackContext)` directly and are NOT wrapped in `ContentstackProvider`.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) wire `ContentstackProvider` into the app tree at the page entry point (e.g., wrap the app in `_app.tsx` or `src/pages/[[...slug]].tsx`), or (b) per the prescribed minimal fix, add the `onEntryChange` subscription + merge logic directly to the existing location where `ContentstackContext` is already populated (the existing provider or page wrapper that sets the context value) — this would be ~10 lines and would connect to the existing consumer tree without a new provider component.

issues.description: The `livePreviewData` field on `IContentstackContext` is never populated by any code path (codegraph_query for `livePreviewData` returned zero results) and is never read by `getContentByKey`/`getValue`. The prescribed fix states 'useContent→getContentByKey returns the preview data instead of the published data' — but `getValue(content, path, defaultValue)` traverses the context object by dot-path (e.g., `page.0.title`). Adding a separate `livePreviewData` map does not cause `getValue` to return preview data for existing paths. The field is dead weight that gives a false impression of compliance.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the `livePreviewData` field. Instead, merge incoming draft content directly into the existing context fields (e.g., `page`, `header`) so that `getValue` traversing paths like `page.0.title` naturally returns the preview value.

issues.description: CONCISION & REUSE: The `useContentstack` hook (lines 51-53) duplicates what `useContent` already does (`useContext(ContentstackContext)`) and has zero callers per codegraph_query. The diff adds 35+ lines of new code (provider component, new hook, new interface) that are all unused dead code. A more concise change: add only the `onEntryChange` subscription + data-merge logic to the existing location where `ContentstackContext` is populated — ~10 lines that would actually connect to the existing consumer tree.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `useContentstack` entirely. Remove `ContentstackProvider` and `IContentstackProviderProps`. Instead, add the `onEntryChange` subscription + merge logic directly in the existing provider/page wrapper that already sets `ContentstackContext` value.

issues.description: No test coverage for live preview behavior. `resolve_test_file` found `src/context/contentstackContext.spec.ts` exists, but given the implementation is entirely non-functional (no-op callback, dead provider, unread field), no test can verify any of the 5 verification criteria. The acceptance criteria require: (VC1) changed entry reflects on page, (VC2) other entries unchanged, (VC3) nav bar reflects change, (VC4) non-preview shows published values, (VC5) disconnect/error shows last values. None are demonstrably met.
issues.suggestedFix: After implementing the actual merge logic, add unit tests in `src/context/contentstackContext.spec.ts` that: (1) verify `onEntryChange` callback merges draft data into context, (2) verify `getContentByKey` returns preview data after merge, (3) verify non-merged fields remain unchanged, (4) verify error/disconnect leaves last values intact.

issues.description: `useState(() => { ... })` is used as a side-effect hook. `useState` initializer is for computing initial state, not for registering callbacks. React may call the initializer multiple times in StrictMode, leading to duplicate `onEntryChange` registrations. Should use `useEffect` with empty dependency array and a cleanup function that unregisters the callback.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace `useState(() => { ... })` with `useEffect(() => { const uid = onEntryChange(callback); return () => { /* unregister using uid */ }; }, [])`.

issues.description: Uses `require()` with an eslint-disable comment instead of a proper ES import. This bypasses TypeScript type checking and tree-shaking. The package `@contentstack/live-preview-utils` is available (verified via dependency_available) and should be imported normally.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace `const livePreviewUtils = require('@contentstack/live-preview-utils')` with a top-level `import ContentstackLivePreview from '@contentstack/live-preview-utils'` (or named import per the package's export shape).

issues.description: TypeScript strict compliance: `footer?: [any]` uses untyped `any` without an explanatory comment. Also `livePreviewData?: Record<string, any>` uses `any`. Per review criteria, no untyped `any` without an explanatory comment.
issues.suggestedFix: Define a proper interface for the footer type, or add an explanatory comment: `// Contentstack footer schema is not yet typed — tracked in AMSD-XXXX`.

issues.suggestedFix: Replace the no-op callback with logic that retrieves the updated entry data from the Contentstack Live Preview SDK (e.g., via `ContentstackLivePreview.getPreviewData()` or equivalent) and merges it into the existing context value by entry UID, so that `getContentByKey`/`getValue` traverses the merged object and returns preview data for the changed entry's paths (e.g., `page.0.title`).

Without wrapping the app tree in this provider, the `onEntryChange` subscription in its `useEffect` never runs, and no live preview data ever reaches any consumer. The provider is never integrated into `_app.tsx` or any layout wrapper.
issues.suggestedFix: Either wrap the app tree in `ContentstackProvider` (e.g., in `_app.tsx` or the root layout), OR — preferred per the prescribed minimal fix — add the `onEntryChange` subscription + data-merge logic directly to the existing location where `ContentstackContext` is already populated (the existing provider or page wrapper that sets the context value), avoiding a new dead component entirely.

The `getValue` util (`src/utils/getValue.ts:10`) traverses the context object by dot-path (e.g., `page.0.title`) — it has no knowledge of a `livePreviewData` map and no merge logic overlays preview data onto published fields. Adding a separate field that nothing writes to or reads from gives a false impression of compliance. This is dead weight.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the `livePreviewData` field. Instead, merge incoming draft content directly into the existing context fields (e.g., update `page`, `header`) so `getValue` naturally traverses the merged data and returns preview values for existing paths.

issues.description: CONCISION & REUSE: The new `useContentstack` hook (lines 51-55) duplicates the existing `useContent` hook at `src/hooks/useContent.ts:5`, which already does `useContext(ContentstackContext)` and is imported by 8+ components across the codebase. CodeGraph query for `useContentstack` callers returned 'Symbol not found' — it is never imported anywhere. This is unused dead code that increases maintenance surface for zero benefit.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `useContentstack`. The existing `useContent` hook already provides access to the context. No new hook is needed.

issues.description: CONCISION & REUSE: The diff adds 35+ lines of new code (a `ContentstackProvider` component, a `useContentstack` hook, an `IContentstackProviderProps` interface) that are ALL unused dead code — zero callers per CodeGraph. The prescribed minimal fix is ~10 lines: add only the `onEntryChange` subscription + data-merge logic to the EXISTING location where `ContentstackContext` is populated. This would connect to the existing consumer tree without any new components or hooks. issues.suggestedFix: Delete `ContentstackProvider`, `IContentstackProviderProps`, and `useContentstack`. In the existing provider or page wrapper that already sets `ContentstackContext` value, add a `useEffect` that subscribes to `ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange`, retrieves the updated entry data, and merges it into the context state via `setValue`. This is ~10 lines and connects to all existing consumers.

issues.description: Test coverage cannot be verified as adequate — the test file exists (confirmed via `resolve_test_file` and git state shows it as a new file `A`), but since the implementation under test (`ContentstackProvider`, `useContentstack`) is dead code with zero callers, any tests would only test code that is never executed in production. Tests must verify the actual live preview data flow: that when `onEntryChange` fires, the context value updates with merged preview data, and that `getContentByKey`/`getValue` returns the preview value for the changed entry while other entries remain unchanged. Without the merge logic and app-tree integration existing, meaningful tests cannot be written.
issues.suggestedFix: After implementing the prescribed minimal fix (merge logic + integration), write tests that: (1) verify `onEntryChange` callback merges incoming entry data into context state; (2) verify `getContentByKey` returns preview data for the changed entry; (3) verify `getContentByKey` returns unchanged published data for other entries; (4) verify that outside a preview session, published values are returned; (5) verify that on SDK error/disconnect, last-shown values persist.
